---CRITIQUE EV Floored Clean EBITDA Yield---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The EV floor at market equity is a substantive fix to the negative-enterprise-value misranking that plausibly explains the archived EBITDA-yield signals' broken portfolio alphas, but the numerator is a recombination of two already-tested weak constructs and inherits their ~7-11% coverage, so upside is limited.

---CRITIQUE Industry Clean Earnings Yield---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is the archived "One Sided Accrual Capped Earnings Yield" wrapped in a standard industry demean — a cosmetic transformation of an existing archive entry, and intra-industry value (Asness-Porter-Stevens) is itself a published anomaly rather than a new mechanism.

---CRITIQUE High Yield Operating Accrual Trap---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Economically this is the Sloan operating-accrual anomaly restricted to high E/P firms (a well-documented value-accrual interaction), and mechanically the double indicator sets the signal to exactly zero for the large majority of firms, so the "long" leg is a mass of ties and portfolio composition will be unstable.

---CRITIQUE EBITDA Supplier Stretch Trap---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Same degenerate construction as the prior proposal (most firms pinned at exactly zero) compounded by apalch's already-thin ~6% coverage, and the underlying payables-stretch mechanism has already failed twice in the archive without diagnosis of why.

---CRITIQUE Tax Paid Earnings Yield---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 1
RATIONALE: Delta taxes payable is tiny relative to income for almost all firms, so ib - max(0, Δtxp) over market equity will be near-perfectly correlated with plain earnings yield — this is effectively a rediscovery of E/P with a negligible perturbation.

---CRITIQUE Accrual Stability Book Yield---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: Penalizing the valuation denominator by scaled accrual volatility is a structurally different construction from the archive's numerator-adjustment attempts and is dimensionally coherent, though the three-annual-observation volatility estimate is noisy and the signal risks being dominated by B/M with the accrual-quality term contributing little variation.
